description: Repeals the Carbon Charge from Saskatoon Light & Power rates.
City Solicitor to amend Bylaw No. 2685.

chips.text: Saskatoon Light & Power customers will no longer pay the Carbon Charge.

description: Funds $598,600 for Pinehouse Drive storm sewer upgrades.
Allocates $70,000 for Sunrise non-potable water study.
Provides $135,000 for Home Energy Loan Program study.

chips.text: Supports studies and upgrades for water conservation and energy efficiency.

description: Saskatoon will apply for federal funding for biogas and emergency planning.
If successful, $200,000 will fund the Biogas Energy System project.

chips.text: Funding sought from Federation of Canadian Municipalities Green Municipal Fund.
Projects relate to organic waste-to-energy and biogas systems.

description: Saskatoon Fire proposes amendments to the Fire and Protective Services Bylaw.
New sewer cleaning billing solution will be created.
Sewer service policy and bylaws will be amended.

chips.text: New sewer billing project funded with $138,000 from reserve.
Residents and businesses with private sewer connections affected.

description: Administration will engage riders on eliminating monthly passes.
Open Payments implementation will continue by end of 2027.
Regular four-year transit fare and UPass reviews begin 2029.

chips.text: University students affected by UPass agreement reviews.
Establishes regular four-year transit fare and UPass reviews.
Administration will report on fare structure changes for 2028-2029 budget.

description: City to negotiate YMCA agreement for East Side Leisure Centre.
Review fundraising, capital costs, and LeisureCard access models.
Investigate swim club contributions for more lap pool lanes.

chips.text: Review of LeisureCard access models may affect users.

description: City will amend land purchase for Holmwood high schools, leisure centre.

chips.text: Future students and east side residents will benefit from the new facilities.

description: Proposes consistent lease rates for Albert Community Centre tenants.
New tenants pay $12.00 per square foot annually immediately.
Existing tenants transition to market rate over two years from 2027.

chips.text: Establishes a single, consistent lease rate structure for all tenants.
Lease rates applied equally to all tenants regardless of legal or tax status.

description: Saskatoon will approve homelessness initiative activities.
Partners with Saskatchewan Housing Corporation.
Establishes a $1,300,000 capital project.
Administration will pursue additional funding.

chips.text: $1,300,000 capital project funded by Saskatchewan Housing Corporation.
Supports unsheltered homeless individuals and addresses encampments.

description: Clint Weiland reappointed to Airport Authority until 2030 meeting.
Appoints 11 members to the Board of Revision for 2027.

chips.text: Eleven individuals, including Shane Keating and Kojo Anaman, are appointed to the Board.

description: Appoints Evan Reekie, Ron Clark to Development Appeals Board until 2028.
Lee Bichel will be reappointed as agency representative.
Represents Ministry of Corrections Policing and Public Safety.
Term on the Committee extends to end of 2027.
Wastewater Biosolids Pipeline budget will increase by $21.6 million.
Funds will shift from two other wastewater projects.
This uses $19.5 million from capital reserve, $2.1 million debt.

chips.text: Decreases two other wastewater projects by $15.6 million and $3.9 million.

description: City will repeal Residential Parking Program Bylaw.
Traffic Bylaw and City Administration Bylaw will be amended.
City Council will consider amending heritage property rules.
Bylaw No. 10234 will amend the Traffic Bylaw.
